## TL;DR

Task #1154 corrects the installed-update restart experience for hand-run and supervised servers, fixes CLI authentication and linked-worktree targeting, and reports restart failures instead of leaving the UI stuck. Review passes identified additional edge cases around helper failures, idle waits, duplicate controls, supervisor polling, and screenshot stability; those are now addressed. The latest `repoos check --changed main` passed, including the scoped remote test/build gate and local UI, docs, formatting, and lint checks.

## Work and rationale

The restart notice now distinguishes supervised servers, hand-run servers, and uncertain supervisor detection. A supervised server gets one pair of restart actions. A hand-run server gets one pair plus a plain explanation that RepoOS relaunches it from the recorded serve flags and port. When an idle restart is pending, both restart actions are disabled and Cancel remains available. An uncertain supervisor is refused with an explanation and a scoped CLI fallback rather than being promised an automatic restart. The modal also reports active agents/checks and explains brief interruption and agent resumption.

The server now starts a detached CLI helper for hand-run restarts. It passes the serving checkout root and bound port, captures helper output, and publishes spawn or exit failures in update status so the UI can clear its busy state and show a command to run manually. Idle checks are shared by both restart types; cancellation stops the idle timer. Missing port information fails closed rather than potentially selecting another server. The server caches the supervisor result, kind, platform and reason together for ten seconds; the frequent app status poll and idle timer no longer repeat synchronous supervisor detection per request.

`repoos restart` now scopes itself to an explicit `--root` when supplied and uses the mode-0600 local token only for its loopback status check. This supports a server started from a linked worktree while preserving the token middleware’s loopback restriction. The CLI help and user documentation list `--root`, `--port`, `--force`, and `--when-idle`. Existing managed-service restart behavior remains on its prior path.

Tests cover hand-run, launchd, systemd, managed, and uncertain supervisor classification; supervised restart route behavior; helper spawn and exit failures; missing-port refusal; idle waiting; cache reuse; and exact dialog action counts. The CLI test verifies that `--root` is used to load configuration, locate the server, read its token, call the restart path, and that the HTTP request includes `x-repoos-local-token` over `127.0.0.1`. The notice screenshot fixture suppresses the unrelated dashboard decision digest request so the capture does not report a transient “Loading…” state.

## Approaches tried

The first restart implementation treated a child process `spawn` event as an accepted action. Review showed that acceptance was insufficient: a later refusal or non-zero exit could leave the old server running while the UI remained disabled. The helper now captures bounded output and reports command failure through update status, while the UI has a reconnect timeout and manual fallback.

The initial hand-run UI used a generic restart pair followed by a second hand-run pair. The controls now branch explicitly: supervised actions are rendered only for supervised servers, and the hand-run block owns its single action pair. Review also found that `getInstalledUpgradeStatus` refreshed the supervisor classification outside the cache; the result object is now cached and reused as a unit.

The screenshot verifier exposed a separate dashboard spinner during the restart-dialog capture. The named restart fixtures now seed a neutral decision digest rather than starting a request unrelated to the captured state. The action tests assert exact labels and counts so future template branches cannot silently add duplicate controls.

## Challenges and blockers

Restart is inherently asynchronous because the helper must stop the current server before relaunching it. The HTTP response confirms that the helper started, while later helper output or reconnect timeout communicates failure. The current server can report an exit failure only while it remains available; the UI timeout provides the fallback if the server goes away before that result can be polled.

Supervisor detection invokes platform process tools synchronously, so making every status poll repeat it could block the server request loop. Caching its full classification for ten seconds avoids repeated work without losing the reason needed for uncertain cases. The change uses the existing cache lifetime rather than adding a new setting.

The final requested check ran the scoped changed-path suite remotely and local gates on this worktree. The remote build/typecheck and tests passed. Local format, lint, build, contrast, UI smoke, and user-docs build passed. The separate focused test run also passed all relevant restart route, UI, and CLI tests.

## Key learnings

A process spawn event says that a process started, not that the requested restart succeeded. The request root and port are part of the identity of a RepoOS server; defaults that point to the board checkout can select the wrong lock when a linked worktree serves the app. Local credentials should remain bound to loopback even when the server advertises a remote address. Finally, UI review should assert the number and state of action controls, not merely find one matching button, and screenshot fixtures should neutralize unrelated in-flight work on the captured route.
